LLM_description:
Situation:
A severe weather system has disrupted ground access across the operational area. Supply Depot Alpha (airfield logistics hub) and Supply Depot Bravo (port and rail yard) are functioning as primary staging points. Forward Relief Units Echo, Foxtrot, and Golf are operating from dispersed localities with constrained road access. Valley corridors remain intermittently blocked by landslides and debris; river crossings are weight-restricted and subject to periodic closure. Security posture requires convoy escorts and daily route clearance on certain corridors. Fuel availability is sufficient for sustained convoy operations, but driver hours and daylight restrictions limit movement windows. Relief commodities are multi-category with differing space and weight characteristics, and available stock varies by depot and by day.

Mission:
Deliver prioritized life-sustaining relief commodities from Supply Depot Alpha and Supply Depot Bravo to Forward Relief Units Echo, Foxtrot, and Golf over the current operational window while minimizing total operational cost, to include transport costs, vehicle deployment costs, fixed route security risk overhead, and penalties for any unavoidable shortfalls. Maintain safe, reliable corridors and ensure equitable support across all forward units.

Execution/Concept:
- Multi-commodity, multi-depot, multi-period distribution. Dispatch plans will be issued for each route-day and commodity, aligning flows with evolving depot stock and unit needs.
- Depot throughput is capped by available stock per commodity per day; shipments from each depot will not exceed on-hand quantities shown in the annex.
- Unit requirements are daily targets; any deficit will be recorded as a controlled shortfall and penalized to reflect humanitarian impact. Shortfalls are a last resort when route risk, transport, and fleet constraints preclude full delivery.
- Vehicle loading is constrained by standard capacity. Commodity volume factors will be applied when converting flows to vehicle loads; total loaded volume per route-day cannot exceed assigned vehicles times capacity.
- Fleet management: The total number of vehicles deployed across all routes on a given day cannot exceed the available fleet. Each deployed vehicle incurs an operating cost.
- Route activation and security overhead: A route must be formally activated to move any vehicles on that route-day. Activating a route (sending any vehicles) triggers a fixed Risk Cost that represents escort teams, route clearance, and security overwatch, and this cost is incurred regardless of the number of vehicles moved on that route-day. No vehicles may be assigned to a route that is not activated.
- Transport costs vary by lane and day; these are applied to the volume of commodities transported. Routing will favor corridors that balance lower transport cost and acceptable risk, subject to stock availability and fleet limits.
- Prioritization: Life-saving commodities and hardest-hit locations will be prioritized. When activation and transport costs outweigh penalty costs for lower-priority items, controlled deferral may be used to preserve fleet and security resources for critical deliveries.
- Contingencies: If primary corridors close, alternate inland routes will be considered, acknowledging higher transport costs and potentially higher risk. Pre-positioning at forward units will be used where stock and access allow to reduce second-day activation requirements.
